summary: All four cycle-1 critical findings and three of four cycle-1 major findings are resolved. One cycle-1 minor finding (Task 5 placeholder spec path) is unresolved and remains minor. One new minor finding surfaced (stale 'WARN + metric capture' phrasing on Task 6 edge-case line 143 — narrative-only, no AC/test impact). No new critical or major findings.

fixes_verified.detail: Task 6 line 26+32+50+77+121+137 explicitly removes MeterRegistry and substitutes a single greppable WARN log line `"bot-connect brute-force counter Redis failure (fail-open)"` asserted via Logback `ListAppender`. Task 8 line 79 renames the IT to `postConnect_redisDown_failsOpen_connectSucceeds_warnLogged` (the `_metricIncremented` suffix is gone). Task 8 line 102 AC says 'No Micrometer assertion — Task 6 does not inject MeterRegistry'. Task 8 line 175 explicitly says 'Do NOT read a Micrometer counter'. Both tasks reference the exact same string literal for the WARN line — `grep` confirms three occurrences in T6 and two in T8 of the identical phrase. Contract drift fully closed.

fixes_verified.fix: T6 ↔ T8 event metadata shape (ip/userAgent are top-level, not in metadata Map)
fixes_verified.detail: Task 6 line 156 reaffirms `bot_connected` metadata = `{projectId, telegramBotId, telegramUsername}` and `bot_disconnected` = `{projectId, telegramBotId, webhookDeleted}`. Task 8 line 110 AC now reads: 'integration test asserts the emitted bot_connected event has metadata map = {projectId, telegramBotId, telegramUsername}. ip and userAgent are TOP-LEVEL fields on the Event document (set by EventService.logEvent(userId, eventType, ipAddress, userAgent, metadata)) — asserted via evt.getIpAddress() / evt.getUserAgent(), NOT via the metadata map.' Task 8 line 184 implementation hint matches. Three-way agreement (T6 ↔ T8 ↔ EventService signature).

Task 5 frontmatter line 3: `depends_on: [4]`. Wave still 1 — task-creator chose declaration over wave-promotion, which is acceptable given the orchestrator can sequence intra-wave by depends_on. Task 5 still consumes Task 4's `bot.subnav.*` and `bot.placeholder` keys; the declared dependency now makes the producer→consumer relationship machine-readable.

Task 2 frontmatter line 3: `depends_on: [1]`. Wave still 1. The `application.properties` shared-edit conflict between T1 and T2 is now expressed by the dependency declaration. T2 still keeps the `@Value('${app.telegram.base-url:https://api.telegram.org}')` default as belt-and-suspenders. Resource-sharing contract closed.

fixes_verified.fix: T4 ↔ T9 disconnect modal key namespace aligned (dot-segmented bot.disconnect.modal.*)
fixes_verified.detail: Task 4 lines 55-56, 89, 95, 184-185, 207-209, 270-272 all use dot-segmented `bot.disconnect.modal.{title,body,confirm,cancel}` and explicitly forbid the camelCase compound root `bot.disconnectModal.*`. Task 9 line 161, 166, 172 use the same dot-segmented namespace and call out the canonical form. Both tasks reference the same anchor (AC19). Vue-i18n key lookup will now succeed in production.

fixes_verified.fix: Task 6 verify: [] aligned with Verification Steps sections
fixes_verified.detail: Task 6 frontmatter line 6: `verify: []`. Verification Steps section contains only an Automated subsection (Gradle test invocation + unit-test coverage description). HTML comment on line 124 explicitly states 'No Verify-smoke and no Verify-user specified in tech-spec for Task 6 — tech-spec line 535's Verify-smoke entry is in fact a description of the unit-test coverage above'. Frontmatter and section content now match.

fixes_verified.fix: Task 11 focus area 5 no longer mentions a required Micrometer counter
fixes_verified.detail: Task 11 line 135 says: 'D14's Micrometer counter expectation is deferred from epic 06 per Task 6's deviation (no Spring Boot Actuator / Micrometer dependency on the project). The audit MUST NOT fail the feature for the missing Micrometer counter; record it as Info / deferred only.' The audit guidance is now consistent with the implementation contract in Tasks 6 and 8 — auditor will not be misled into flagging the missing counter as a critical finding.

findings.issue: Task 5 TDD Anchor (line 51) still references `frontend/tests/pages/projects/bot.spec.ts::placeholder renders SettingsSubnav` (placed at `tests/pages/projects/bot.spec.ts`), while Task 9 'Files to modify' (line 29, 43, 48, 50–67, 101, 121) places its full bot-page spec at `frontend/tests/pages/projects/[projectId]/settings/bot.spec.ts` (one level deeper, under `[projectId]/settings/`). Two different files. Cycle-1 minor finding #2 is still unresolved. Risk: Task 9 either has to delete Task 5's smoke spec or leave a stale file behind. The pnpm parity gate will not catch this.
findings.fix: Either (a) change Task 5 line 51 to use the deeper path `frontend/tests/pages/projects/[projectId]/settings/bot.spec.ts` so Task 9 cleanly replaces it, or (b) document in Task 9 'What to do' that the file at `tests/pages/projects/bot.spec.ts` is deleted as part of Task 9's setup. (a) is simpler; (b) requires no Task-5 edit but adds an extra step to Task 9.

findings.issue: Task 6 Edge cases line 143 says 'Redis unreachable on DEL after successful Connect: must not fail the Connect — counter expires naturally after 15 min; WARN + metric capture the failure.' The 'WARN + metric' wording is leftover from the prior Micrometer contract — there is no metric in the implementation any more (Description, ACs, TDD Anchor, Verification Steps all explicitly removed the counter). This is a stale phrase in narrative text only, not in any AC or test; severity minor because no test or implementer-action follows from this line. But a reviewer reading bottom-up could be misled.
findings.fix: Edit Task 6 line 143 to drop the 'metric capture' phrase: 'Redis unreachable on DEL after successful Connect: must not fail the Connect — counter expires naturally after 15 min; WARN log line emitted (via Logback ListAppender-asserted message — see Description).'

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria — JSON wire format / tech-spec documentation hygiene
findings.issue: Cycle-1 finding #10 (tech-spec D14-style: tech-spec Task 3 entry does not mention @JsonValue lowercase serialisation, but Task 3 implements it). Still unresolved at the task-file layer (Task 3 itself encodes the contract correctly). This is a tech-spec hygiene issue, not a task issue — flagging only because the cycle-1 report listed it; no blocker for execution.
findings.fix: After Wave 4 lands, update tech-spec.md Implementation Tasks Task 3 entry to mention the @JsonValue lowercase serialisation contract. Not a task-file blocker.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria — deviation from tech-spec D14
findings.issue: Cycle-1 finding #11 (tech-spec D14 mandates a Micrometer counter, Task 6 intentionally drops it, Task 6 AC11 acknowledges the deviation). The cross-task contract between T6 and T8 is now consistent (fix verified above), but tech-spec D14 still on paper requires the Micrometer counter. Recommended (out of scope of cross-task review): edit tech-spec D14 to drop 'Micrometer counter' and replace with 'dedicated greppable WARN log line'. Until then, Post-completion step on Task 6 ('If deviated from spec — describe deviation and reason') will capture the deviation in decisions.md.
findings.fix: (Optional, post-wave-5) Edit tech-spec D14 to remove the Micrometer counter requirement and align with the WARN-log contract. This is documentation cleanup, not a task-file fix.

checks_passed.detail: TokenEncryptor owner T1 → consumer T6; TelegramApiClient owner T2 → consumer T6; BotRepository owner T3 → consumer T6; application.properties shared edit owner T1 → consumer T2 (now declared via T2 depends_on [1]); i18n bot.* keys owner T4 → consumers T5, T9 (T5 declares depends_on [4]; T9 declares depends_on [4]).

No two tasks in the same wave create their own instance of any shared resource. Wave-1 application.properties edits are owned by T1; Wave-1 i18n locale-file edits are owned by T4; Wave-2 BotService is the sole consumer of T1/T2/T3 Wave-1 outputs.

W1=[1,2,3,4,5]; W2=[6,7]; W3=[8,9]; W4=[10,11,12]; W5=[13]. All depends_on values reference existing tasks with strictly lower waves OR same-wave intra-wave dependency (T2→[1] same wave, T5→[4] same wave — both acceptable when orchestrator honours depends_on within the wave). T6→[1,2,3] (W1→W2 ✓), T7→[3] (W1→W2 ✓), T8→[6] (W2→W3 ✓), T9→[4,5,7] (W1,W1,W2 → W3 ✓), T10/11/12→[8,9] (W3→W4 ✓), T13→[10,11,12] (W4→W5 ✓). No cycles.
T3 implements @JsonValue lowercase + @JsonCreator lowercase parsing; T7 declares the lowercase literal union; T8 IT asserts lowercase JSON. Three layers agree.
T2 scrubber regex `\d{1,20}:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,50}` matches T6 negative-assertion regex and T9 DOM-negative-assertion regex `/\d{1,20}:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,50}/`. Consistent.
T6 and T8 both specify `${app.url}/webhooks/telegram/{projectId}`; T8 IT asserts the exact URL is sent to MockWebServer for setWebhook.

T6 emits `bot_connected` and `bot_disconnected` only; metadata maps are explicitly `{projectId, telegramBotId, telegramUsername}` and `{projectId, telegramBotId, webhookDeleted}`. T8 IT asserts the same shape with `ip`/`userAgent` checked as top-level Event document fields via `evt.getIpAddress()` / `evt.getUserAgent()`. No `bot_test_message_sent` event.

T6 emits a single dedicated WARN string `"bot-connect brute-force counter Redis failure (fail-open)"` from BotService logger on both INCR-failure and DEL-failure paths; asserted via Logback `ListAppender<ILoggingEvent>`. T8 IT asserts the SAME exact string via the SAME `ListAppender` pattern. No Micrometer / MeterRegistry / actuator on either side. Tech-spec D14 deviation is intentional and consistent across tasks.

T4 owns the full inventory: `bot.page.*`, `bot.connectForm.*`, `bot.connected.*`, `bot.disconnect.modal.{title,body,confirm,cancel}` (DOT-segmented, NOT camelCase), `bot.toasts.*`, `bot.subnav.{general,bot}`, `bot.placeholder`, `errors.bot.connect.{400,409,422,429,500,502}`, `errors.bot.disconnect.404`, `errors.bot.testMessage.{422,502}`, `errors.bot.{connect,disconnect,testMessage}.generic`. T5 and T9 consume; T9 line 162-172 inventory matches T4 verbatim. pnpm prebuild parity gate enforces uk↔en symmetry.

T1 `EncryptedValue(byte[] iv, byte[] ciphertext)` is raw bytes by contract. T6 step 2 (line 33) now explicitly: '**Base64-encode both iv and ciphertext with Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(...) before persistence**' and step 4 (line 35) '**Base64-decode** the stored encryptedTokenIv and encryptedTokenCiphertext strings via Base64.getDecoder().decode(...)'. TDD Anchor lines 55-56 add `connect_encryptedTokenAndIvAreBase64EncodedBeforeSave` and `disconnect_base64DecodesIvAndCiphertextBeforeDecrypt` tests. Boundary contract is now explicit and test-anchored.

T8 line 181 specifies class-level static `MockWebServer` (for @DynamicPropertySource compatibility) AND line 182 explicitly mandates per-test isolation: 'in @BeforeEach, drain ALL leftover recorded requests with a zero-timeout loop until null — `while (mockTelegram.takeRequest(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) != null) { /* drain */ }` — AND reset the dispatcher / clear the response queue.' Cross-test contamination risk mitigated with an explicit protocol.

T3 partialFilter uses uppercase `{ 'status': 'CONNECTED' }` matching Java BotStatus.CONNECTED.name(); T13 mongosh smoke asserts the same uppercase. Jackson lowercase wire format is independent of Mongo storage.

T3 declares nullable, T6 disconnect step nulls all four (encryptedTokenCiphertext, encryptedTokenIv, tokenSuffix, webhookSecretHash) plus sets disconnectedAt. T8 IT asserts post-disconnect all four are null.

T13 lines 28, 63, 188, 192 consistently model T10/T11/T12 as `reviewers: []` audit tasks done when the report is produced and committed, with critical findings resolved via follow-up fix-tasks (not review rounds). Cycle-1 finding #11 fully addressed.
